# PR #174 correctness review

**PASS-WITH-NOTES** at `1d9a1f30fbee5b3bce5b09a8bb084947a9dba997`. Source and exact-head CI review is complete.

Scope follows the PM's clarification: a LIVE pre-bind seat must not be tombstoned; entering never_bound during registration is permitted. A present pane vetoes, and the final registry comparison protects a concurrent bind. This answers reviewer request `01a1b8ff-1c23-7e70-a650-ba3a7e555952`.

## Policy and brakes

For proc=None and a recorded pane, confirmed pane absence is the deciding policy. Each brake only spares: a matching pane returns Retain; Ok(None) returns pane-probe-needs-a-launch; a read error returns pane-probe-failed; no recorded pane returns process-identity-unavailable. No unreadable result becomes absence.

The real adapter uses query_live, not query or an ordinary list_panes fallback. query_live cannot start or replace a client; disconnected, disabled, timed-out or unavailable observations defer. Error replies and pane parsing errors remain errors. The default port returns None. The real control-mode test proves cold/disabled and warm reads add no launches.

Successful registration requires a process tuple: register_inner passes proc.is_some() to shared admission, which refuses NoBindEvidence otherwise. An already-registered descriptor therefore uses the unchanged process/pane rule, never never_bound. Spawn creates the pane before writing its proc=None descriptor. A live pre-bind descriptor does enter never_bound but is spared by its present pane. Execution re-observes; the existing atomic raw-descriptor comparison also protects registration or revival that commits before tombstoning.

## N001: exact pre-bind CAS race is not separately tested

No new test in this PR exercises a proc=None-to-Some registration landing after the final pane read and before tombstoning. The passing existing death_sweep_preserves_registration_during_old_process_observation starts with an already-bound seat and pauses its second process observation; registration lands before the later pane read. reap_concurrent_revive_between_observation_and_commit_is_preserved likewise changes an already-bound incarnation during a process probe.

These prove the shared stale-snapshot CAS machinery, not the exact new interleaving requested. Source inspection shows SqliteRegistry::publish_tombstone compares the entire current descriptor against expected under its write transaction before appending the event or updating the row. A committed None-to-Some bind therefore vetoes the stale tombstone. This unchanged generic guard supports the assessment, but the specific pre-bind/pane-read race must not be represented as an executed regression. A focused interleaving witness is a nonblocking proof improvement, not a demonstrated code defect.

## Pane reuse and deployment

A new pane reusing the recorded ID vetoes a never-bound reap, even if unrelated. This is acceptable as a conservative presence brake under the stated policy, not proof of incarnation continuity. Without the old process start there is no existing process-root comparison. Such a dead record may be retained indefinitely while that ID remains present; this PR does not guarantee complete cleanup across pane-ID reuse.

The four reported deployment candidates retire only if the live control client can confirm their panes remain absent and the registry binding is unchanged. No sweep signals a process or destroys a pane. The four-seat inventory and prime ruling A are packet-supplied evidence, not a new live census.

## Lifecycle replacement and held messages

The HTTP test replacement is an intentional contract change, not a weakened always-pass assertion: the same three no-process/recorded-pane fixtures now must be specific never-bound candidates; dry-run keeps before/after=3 and reaped empty; execution must return the same candidates, three reaps and after=0. Restoring the old Unknown behavior fails the candidate assertions. Missing-pane and unreadable cases remain tested independently.

**N002, documentation:** the /v1/reap invariants in crates/testkit/fixtures/golden/api/governance-routes.json still describe bound-process-only eligibility. The executable replacement and API documentation encode the new branch; the fixture's invariant prose should also name it. Its sample response is not fresh runtime proof.

The canonical reaper/store path does not delete ordinary queued jobs. The real-store digest test proves a tombstoned recipient's ordinary job remains queued while its hold leaves the live fleet's digest, with a live recipient as a positive inclusion control. This concerns held delivery diagnostics, not pending FYIs: the existing tombstone transaction drops pending FYIs separately.

F115 reuses flag_shown after dormant wake admission. It flags exactly the view's held-job IDs only for delivered/queued/held outcomes; refused/error outcomes do not flag. A failed flag write logs explicitly and can permit repeats. The two-wake regression first proves the hold was shown, then re-arms and proves it is not repeated.

## Mutation evidence

Author-supplied executed witnesses, not reviewer-local reruns:

- Changing no-control-client Ok(None) to a never-bound absent Candidate fails a_never_bound_seat_is_reaped_only_when_its_recorded_pane_is_absent, specifically its without_control_client case, which expects no candidate and pane-probe-needs-a-launch.
- Restoring the old Unknown fails both the never-bound brake/candidate test and the death-sweep integration test.
- Removing dormant flag_shown fails a_dormant_wake_shows_each_held_message_once, whose second digest must omit the already-shown message.

Tapir supplied the concrete mutations, command selectors and failure summaries in message `3d206a98-ab5d-4ee2-807e-1094f81b79e3`. These were run on the uncommitted working tree later committed as 5ff9ec5c; no independent saved assertion log exists. Reviewer git diff confirmed reaper.rs, reaper_tests.rs, pa_presence.rs, pa_watchdog.rs and pa_watchdog_tests.rs are byte-identical between 5ff9ec5c and this frozen head. Source inspection confirms each witness would reject the stated mutant. This transfers the author witness to the reviewed source but does not turn it into reviewer-executed mutation proof.

## CI, cost and limits

Exact-head CI [42438560763](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42438560763), attempt 1, passed Rust lint, Rust tests and Node 22/24 checks. JUnit artifact 13600641909 contains 2199 executed cases, zero failures/errors. It includes all new reaper, lifecycle HTTP, real-control-client and dormant/digest controls, plus existing concurrent registration/revive, process/pane brake and one-time death-observation tests.

The existing death sweep defaults to one tick every 5 seconds. Each no-process seat with a recorded pane adds one live-control list query per observation; an execution candidate is queried again before CAS. Registered seats do not use this new read. No new loop, timer or process launch site exists. Dormant wake adds one held-delivery flag write per admitted digest containing holds, once per dormant stretch (normally at least 30 minutes), per PA. Live fleet CPU/RSS/spawn measurement remains performance-owned and was not run here.

No local product builds/tests or mutations, dependency changes, live reaps/censuses or product edits were performed. Checkout is clean/detached and matches the remote exact head; GitHub reports CLEAN.
